newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids again buoyed by firmer crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids again buoyed by firmer crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices, again buoyed by another rally in crude, held mostly steady Tuesday, but activity remained light ahead of the New Year's holiday Wednesday, industry sources said.

"There hasn't been much going on this week, but people are watching crude and the (cold) weather in Europe," said one cash trader, adding hopes for exports overseas helped underpin the complex this week, particularly at the Gulf, despite forecasts for mild East Coast weather later this week and next.
New York Harbor one pct was steady at $21.00-25 a barrel, with January paper up a quarter with crude to $20.50-75.
Traders said February one percent paper gained a similar amount to the low-$20 area.
High sulphurs in New York again notionally were unchanged.
At the U.S. Gulf Coast, prices were stable to firmer, with one percent unchanged to slightly higher at $18.75-19.00 and three percent up modestly at $16.50, traders said.

Traders said 60,000 barrels of high quality, USG three percent sold Monday at $16.40 (prompt). Two USG high sulphur deals were reported Tuesday, one for 100,000 barrels sold by a refiner, but other details could not be confirmed.
New York city gate gas prices firmed 10-20 cents Tuesday to the $3.60s/mmBtu level versus NYH one percent resid still at a $3.35/mmBtu equivalent.
